objectives: Describe the three phases of the PLC scan cycle and how often OpenPLC runs it in CybICS
Predict what the CybICS compressor rule does for a given HPT pressure, including the hysteresis between 60 and 90
Explain why a forged coil is overwritten by the next scan while a forged register is overwritten by hwio
Explain why anyone who reaches the PLC can change its values, and why a new program is the most powerful change
takeaways: A PLC repeats one scan every 50 ms: read inputs, run the program on that snapshot, write outputs.
A forged value lasts only until its owner writes again: the scan for coil 1, hwio for the pressure.
Modbus reaches coils and registers without a password, and a new program changes the plant for good.

checkpoints.question: During phase 2 of a scan, the real pressure changes. When does the program see the new value?
options: At once, because the program reads the live sensor value
In the next scan, when phase 1 takes a fresh copy of the inputs
In phase 3 of this scan, when inputs and outputs are synced
checkpoints.explanation: The program works on the snapshot taken in phase 1, so a change during the program waits for the next read-inputs phase, at most one scan (50 ms in CybICS) later. It does not read the live sensor line by line, and phase 3 only writes outputs; it reads nothing.

quiz.question: The plant is in automatic mode, the compressor is running and the HPT pressure has risen to 75. What does the compressor rule decide in the next scan?
options: Stop it, because 75 is above the start threshold of 60
Keep it running, because it is on and 75 is below 90
Stop it, because 75 is inside the healthy pressure band
Nothing, the rule only runs when a threshold is crossed
quiz.explanation: The seal-in branch (hpt < 90 AND compressorState = 1) keeps it running until 90. Stopping once the pressure is above 60 is the tempting mistake: it ignores the hysteresis that stops the compressor from switching on and off every scan. The rule runs on every scan, not only on crossings.

quiz.question: An attacker uses Modbus to switch coil 1 (the compressor) off while the plant is in automatic mode and the logic wants it on. What happens?
options: It stays off until an operator turns it on at the HMI
The next scan turns it back on, within about 50 ms
hwio restores the coil about 20 ms later
The PLC rejects the write, because coils are outputs
quiz.explanation: The program owns coil 1 and assigns it on every scan in automatic mode, so the write lasts at most one scan. hwio is tempting because it is fast, but it only reads the coils and never writes them; it owns the pressure registers instead. Modbus does accept writes to coils.

quiz.question: An attacker wants to switch the compressor coil off over Modbus. What do they need?
options: The operator's password for the HMI
A copy of the PLC's plant program file
Nothing but a network path to the PLC
A login on the engineering workstation
quiz.explanation: Modbus asks for no password: anyone who reaches the PLC can write its coils and registers. The HMI password is tempting, but it only protects FUXA's screens, not the PLC behind them. Neither the program nor a workstation login is needed to send a single write.

quiz.question: Which of these happen when the `manual` register is set to a non-zero value?
options: The automatic block stops writing the three plant coils
The heartbeat on coil 0 keeps blinking
The program switches every output off until manual is cleared
A coil written over Modbus keeps its value
quiz.explanation: The automatic block is wrapped in IF manual < 1 with no ELSE, so the compressor, system valve and refill coils are left alone and keep whatever was written to them; the heartbeat is outside that block. Switching every output off is what the stop register does, not manual.

quiz.question: To keep a forged HPT pressure in register 1126, how often does an attacker have to write it?
options: Once; the PLC never changes a register it only reads
Faster than every 50 ms, so it lands before each PLC scan
Faster than hwio rewrites it, about every 20 ms
Once per second, to match the HMI poll
quiz.explanation: It is true that the program only reads 1126, but hwio, the plant simulation, writes the real value back about every 20 ms. Beating the 50 ms PLC scan is the tempting answer, but it is hwio's rewrite the attacker has to outpace, not the PLC.
